Evidence in Action – Case Study 002

Last Energy

Supporting the Welsh Government Last Energy Task and Finish Group through evidence-based industrial intelligence.

The Challenge
Wales needed to understand the manufacturing capability that could support a future Last Energy supply chain — not simply identify companies already working in offshore wind.

The Intelligence
GSCI combined manufacturing knowledge, supplier intelligence and direct engagement. Last Energy was introduced to local stakeholders, potential sites were explored, supplier events were organised in Cardiff and Swansea, and targeted one-to-one meetings and company visits connected the developer with Welsh capability.

The Outcome
As Welsh capability became visible, Last Energy’s expected Welsh content increased from approximately 10% to 80% — demonstrating the potential value of active supply-chain intelligence and engagement.

TURNING CAPABILITY INTO OPPORTUNITY
10% → 80%
Initial expected Welsh content → potential Welsh content identified through engagement

What Changed?

The project moved from a relatively modest expectation of Welsh participation to a much broader understanding of the manufacturing, engineering and supply-chain capability available in Wales.

Why It Matters

The opportunity was not simply about identifying suppliers. Direct engagement, events, introductions and site visits helped turn industrial capability into a credible proposition for inward investment.

Evidence at a Glance

  • Client: Last Energy
  • Programme: Last Energy Task and Finish Group
  • Engagement: Cardiff and Swansea supplier events, one-to-ones and site visits
  • Methodology: manufacturing intelligence, supplier engagement and capability matching
  • Strategic contribution: potential Welsh content increased from approximately 10% to 80%
